newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Siemens, Matsushita mull Portugal factory.
newsitem.headline: Siemens, Matsushita mull Portugal factory.

text.p: German group Siemens and Japan's Matsushita have submitted a joint investment proposal to the Portuguese government to build a 10 billion escudo ($64 million) electronic components factory, a spokesman said.

The proposal to build the factory near Evora in the depressed Alentejo region, which has no formal timetable, was delivered to the Economy Ministry earlier this month, Siemens spokesman Hans Muller told Reuters.
"We intend to invest in a new plant, and it could be in Portugal," Muller told Reuters. "Siemens will consider Portugal as well as other countries as possible sites."
Muller said the factory, which would be operated by a joint venture owned equally by Siemens and Matsushita and could create 400 jobs, would export a large proportion of its production.
A decision to proceed with the investment would depend partially on any incentives that the Socialist government would be prepared to offer, Muller said.
The joint venture is called Siemens Matsushita Components GmbH.
Siemens presently operates five factories in Portugal and is building a sixth, a memory chips factory in northern Portugal, the second biggest foreign investment in the country.
